proposed statement: Parents struggle to get information from the school because fee statements are printed and sent home in learners' bags but half never reach parents
key statement: SchoolBase 7 (from about 2014) runs on a server in the admin block. It holds learners, parents, fees and marks, exports CSV, produces the report PDFs, and sends the emails.

proposed statement: The portal must provide the current balance, monthly statement as a PDF, and reference for EFT payment
key statement: No payments through the portal: the school doesn't take card payments and won't; parents keep paying by EFT or debit order.

proposed statement: The portal must be zero-rated by the network to accommodate parents with limited data
key statement: Could the portal be zero-rated with the mobile networks? The consultant will look into it.

proposed statement: The school has only one IT person who works two days a week, so if the portal breaks on report night, there's no one to fix it
key statement: The school has one IT person, two days a week; if something breaks on report night, there is nobody.

proposed statement: The school wants to start with a trial of one grade's term one reports in April to test the portal
key statement: Trial the portal with grade 8's term-one reports in April before the full roll-out, so a bad first report day doesn't cost parents' trust.

proposed statement: If the first report day goes badly, parents lose trust in the portal immediately
key statement: Trial the portal with grade 8's term-one reports in April before the full roll-out, so a bad first report day doesn't cost parents' trust.

proposed statement: The portal's data must be zero-rated by the network to accommodate parents with limited data
key statement: The portal must be light on mobile data (small pages, PDFs downloaded only when opened), because data is expensive for parents (Graham reckons most are on prepaid) and bursary families count every megabyte.

proposed statement: The portal must be able to handle the current parent count of sixteen hundred and fifty, including families with both parents and grandparents listed
key statement: On report day every parent logs in within a couple of hours, mostly in the evening, from about 1,650 parent contacts (corrected from 1,400). Last year a one-grade test of reports on the website took the site down.
